answer: Picture a reef where each new polyp attaches through one shared inlet: every admission cohort receives a single fixed voting weight, divided across the whole meadow of its members. A thousand identities arriving together therefore hold a thousandth of a vote each, so mass registration buys no influence. Standing is earned by passing randomly scheduled peer audits over several epochs, and auditors caught rubber-stamping are slashed. An attacker must pay compute for every identity and bribe many established auditors whose own stake is forfeited when detected.
